title: Unleashing the Caspian’s potential in oil, gas and critical minerals | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Wood Mackenzie argues that with the Iran war lifting energy-security priority, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan could become a reliable supply region by building cross-Caspian oil and gas pipelines to complete a 'Middle Corridor'. Azerbaijan's output is flat at 1.2 million boe/d, Kazakhstan's CPC exports are disrupted, and Turkmenistan sells 34 Bcm/year only to China.

insights.claim: The war in Iran is pushing energy security up government agendas, so importing countries want to diversify oil and gas sources and geopolitically stable Caspian producers (Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan) are positioned to become a bigger reliable supplier.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Caspian upstream and export infrastructure are beneficiaries of supply-security diversification.
insights.locator: As the war in Iran pushes energy security

insights.claim: Azerbaijan's production reached 1.2 million boe/d by 2010 (80% oil), has held there since, and on WoodMac forecasts stays flat to the late 2030s helped by Phase 2 of TotalEnergies' Absheron gas project, which FID'd last month.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Output plateau means gas, not oil, is the growth lever.

insights.claim: Gas has become Azerbaijan's growth story, about 60% of production in 2026.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Azeri gas exports to Europe are rising in importance.
insights.locator: Gas has become the growth story

insights.claim: Azerbaijan has already built export routes (BTC oil pipeline 1.2 million b/d, TANAP and TAP gas pipelines to Europe), but BTC is substantially underutilised even with Kazakh and Turkmen volumes.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Spare BTC capacity lowers the cost of adding cross-Caspian oil.
insights.locator: The construction of major export pipelines

insights.claim: Kazakhstan produces 2.2 million b/d of liquids with over 1.5 million b/d exported via the CPC pipeline to Novorossiysk, but flows have been seriously disrupted by attacks linked to the Russia/Ukraine war.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Kazakh export concentration through Russia is a supply risk that motivates alternative routes.

insights.claim: Kashagan's next phase could lift Kazakh export volumes by more than 0.2 million b/d.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Incremental barrels need export capacity beyond CPC.
insights.locator: There is potential to lift export volumes

insights.claim: Turkmenistan's Galkynysh, the world's second largest gas field, supports exports of 34 Bcm/year sold exclusively to China, well under half of Qatar's North field exports in 2025, with little progress on additional sales.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Single-buyer dependence gives China pricing leverage and strands reserves.
insights.locator: The giant Galkynysh is the second largest gas field

insights.claim: Turkmenistan needs alternative export options to commercialise Galkynysh's vast reserves.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Westbound gas access would be a major reshaping of Eurasian gas flows.
insights.locator: Turkmenistan needs to cultivate alternative export options

insights.claim: Building cross-Caspian oil and gas pipelines linking Kazakh oil and Turkmen gas to Azerbaijan's existing routes would complete a 'Middle Corridor', a new Silk Road for molecules, giving export optionality and energy security while Azerbaijan earns tariffs.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Watch for cross-Caspian pipeline agreements as a leading indicator of re-routed Eurasian flows.
insights.quote: A logical solution for the region is obvious

insights.claim: The Middle Corridor faces unresolved questions: aligning governments including Russia and China, whether Europe will commit to long-term gas contracts, and who finances cross-border infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Execution risk is high; announcements may outrun financing.
insights.quote: Realisation of the concept is far from straight forward.

insights.claim: Central Asian countries are rich in critical minerals and are ramping up efforts to attract foreign investment in mining and processing, with demand pull from both China and the West.
insights.speaker: Simon Flowers
insights.so_what: Secondary opportunity alongside hydrocarbons; the article gives no detail.
insights.locator: The Caspian - an emerging source of critical minerals
